title: Neptune SQ3 Squash (Neptune SQ3 F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Neptune SQ3 squash is an F1 hybrid squash variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Neptune SQ3 squash is an F1 hybrid squash variety, also sold or known as Neptune SQ3 F1 or Neptune F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Neptune SQ3 squash is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Neptune SQ3 F1 or Neptune F1, this is the same squash. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [squash variety finder](/crop-varieties/squash), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).
Key facts about Neptune SQ3 squash

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit squash fields most often: [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly), [squash beetle](/pests/squash-beetle), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Medium to large, high and flat, with yellow orange flesh.
Highly tolerant of cucurbit viruses, its seller says.

blocks.text: Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Neptune SQ3 squash

Choose a fruit size your buyer wants, from small round ones for households to big flat ones for the market. A thick, deep orange flesh keeps longer and sells better. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Neptune SQ3 F1 the same as Neptune SQ3?
items.a: Yes. Neptune SQ3 F1 is another name for Neptune SQ3. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Neptune SQ3?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
